task.title: No Internet Connection
task.shortdesc: Restore Internet access when a connected client device cannot access websites or online services.

prereq.p: Before you troubleshoot the Internet connection:

ul.li: Make sure that the or Optical Network Terminal (ONT) is connected to the ISP service.
Make sure that the is turned on.
Make sure that the client device is connected through Ethernet or Wi-Fi.
Check whether the ISP has reported a service interruption.
Record recent changes to the network configuration.

prereq.note: Make one change at a time. Test the Internet connection after each change.
Do not look into an optical port or the end of a fiber-optic cable. Contact the ISP if the fiber connection requires service.

context.p: A client device can connect to the local network even when the Internet connection is not available. Test the local network before you change the router or client-device settings.
context.note: A Wi-Fi symbol does not always indicate that Internet access is available. The symbol can show only that the device is connected to the router.
Isolate the failure at each network boundary: client device to router, router to modem or ONT, and modem or ONT to the ISP.

step.cmd: Determine which devices have no Internet access.

substep.cmd: Test the Internet connection on another client device.
If available, test one wired device and one wireless device.

ul.li: If only one device is affected, troubleshoot the client device.
If all devices are affected, check the router, modem or ONT, and ISP service.
If only wireless devices are affected, check the Wi-Fi connection and settings.
If only wired devices are affected, check the Ethernet cables and LAN ports.

step.cmd: Check the network connection on the client device.

choices.choice: For a wireless connection, confirm that the device is connected to .
For a wired connection, confirm that the device shows an active Ethernet connection.

info.note: Make sure that the device is not connected to if the guest network has access restrictions or is not operational.

step.stepresult: The client device shows an active local network connection.

step.cmd: Verify that the client device can communicate with the .

substep.cmd: Open a supported web browser.
Go to .
Confirm that the sign-in page for the opens.

info.p: If the sign-in page opens, the client device can communicate with the router.
If the sign-in page does not open, reconnect the client device to the network. Then, test the connection again.

step.stepresult: The client device can access the local network.

step.cmd: Check the status indicators on the or ONT and the .

ul.li: The power indicators show normal operation.
The Internet or service indicator on the modem or ONT shows normal operation.
The WAN indicator on the router shows an active connection.
The applicable LAN or Wi-Fi indicator shows an active connection.

info.note: Indicator names, colors, and patterns can differ by device. Refer to the instructions supplied with the device.

step.cmd: Check the Ethernet connection between the or ONT and the .

substep.cmd: Make sure that one end of the Ethernet cable is fully connected to the Ethernet port on the modem or ONT.
Make sure that the other end is fully connected to the on the router.
Check the cable for visible damage.
Replace the cable with a known working Ethernet cable if necessary.

info.note: Do not connect the modem or ONT to a LAN port on the router.

step.stepresult: The modem or ONT has a working physical connection to the router.

info.p: Use a mobile data connection or another available Internet connection to check the ISP service status.
If the ISP reports a service interruption, wait until the ISP restores the service.
info.note: Contact the ISP if the Internet or service indicator on the modem or ONT shows an error.

substep.cmd: Turn off the client device.
Turn off the .
Turn off the or ONT if the ISP permits this action.
Wait until the devices turn off completely.
Turn on the or ONT.
Wait until the Internet service indicator shows normal operation.
Turn on the .
Wait until the router status indicators show normal operation.
Turn on the client device.

info.note: Do not press the reset button. A factory reset can remove the custom network configuration.

substep.cmd: Connect the client device to or an available LAN port.
Open a supported web browser.
Open a trusted external website.
Confirm that the website opens without an Internet connection error.

step.stepresult: The client device can access Internet services.

step.cmd: Review the Internet connection status in the .

substep.cmd: Go to .
Sign in with the credentials for the .
Open the .
Review the WAN or Internet connection status.
Confirm that the affected client device appears in the connected-device list.

info.p: If the router shows a disconnected WAN status, check the modem or ONT connection and the ISP service.

step.cmd: Verify the network settings on the client device.

substep.cmd: Confirm that the client device has a valid address.
Confirm that the subnet mask is .
Confirm that the default gateway is .
Confirm that a valid DNS server address is assigned.

info.p: If the device uses automatic configuration, the typically assigns an address from .
info.note: The network settings can differ if an administrator changed the default network configuration.

step.cmd: Renew the automatic network settings on the client device.

info.p: Disconnect and reconnect the network connection, or use the operating-system control that renews the DHCP configuration.
Confirm that the assigns a valid address, gateway, and DNS server.

step.cmd: Test gateway connectivity and DNS resolution separately.

substep.cmd: Test communication with .
Test communication with a known external IP address.
Test access to an external destination by its domain name.

ul.li: If the gateway test fails, check the local connection and client network settings.
If the gateway test succeeds but the external IP test fails, check the router WAN connection and ISP service.
If the external IP test succeeds but the domain-name test fails, check the DNS configuration.

info.p: Confirm that the client device or router uses a valid DNS server. The default DNS server defined for this guide is .
info.note: Use only a DNS server approved by the network administrator or ISP.

ul.li: A changed WAN configuration
A changed DNS server
A changed DHCP configuration
A firmware update
A new modem, ONT, router, or gateway
A new access-control or security rule
A changed cable or port

info.p: Reverse only the applicable change and test the Internet connection again.
info.note: Do not restore a configuration that contains insecure settings or known errors.

step.cmd: Check for an approved firmware update for the .

info.p: Use the firmware update function in the or download approved firmware from the .
info.note: Do not turn off the router during a firmware update.
Install only firmware intended for and the applicable .

step.cmd: Test Internet access on at least two client devices.

info.p: Test both wired and wireless connections if both connection types are available.

step.stepresult: The tested client devices can access the local network and Internet services.

result.p: Internet connectivity is restored. The has an active WAN connection, and connected client devices can access Internet services.

postreq.p: If Internet access is not restored, collect the following information:

ul.li: Product model:
Firmware version:
Hardware version:
The status indicator conditions
The devices affected by the problem
The date and time when the problem started
Recent network or configuration changes
Displayed error messages
The troubleshooting steps already completed

postreq.note: Do not send Wi-Fi passwords, administrator passwords, account passwords, or other confidential credentials to technical support.
